items.title: Meta Ads: $198.40 spend (4d catch-up), 11 leads, $18.04 CPL
items.summary: Catch-up window 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-17 (4 days, no prior meta-ads run covered them): Meta spent $198.40, all on the only actively-delivering campaign, Flooring Problems Campaign, generating 11 leads at $18.04 CPL. That's above the 7-day baseline CPL (~$16.64 over $349.45 / 21 leads) but well under the 2x anomaly threshold. Account is ACTIVE and no ads are flagged.

needs_attention: Gap wider than a day: the most recent prior meta-ads.json was 2026-08-14 (run_at 08:46:49), covering yesterday-of-that-run 2026-08-13 only — no meta-ads run happened 2026-08-15 through 2026-08-17. This run widened to --days 4 (2026-08-14 through 2026-08-17, within the 7-day cap) to cover the gap; the spend/leads/CPL above are a 4-day aggregate for that catch-up window, not a single day, because Meta's insights endpoint (level=campaign, no time_increment) returns one combined row per window rather than per-day rows.

Flooring Problems Campaign's raw actions again include lead-like conversion types outside the script's documented LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set (offsite_complete_registration_add_meta_leads, offsite_search_add_meta_leads, offsite_content_view_add_meta_leads — each valued at 11 over the catch-up window / 21 over the 7-day baseline, matching the counted leads exactly both times, same pattern first flagged 2026-08-14). No discrepancy in the counted total either time, but this is now a repeat observation — worth reviewing whether LEAD_ACTION_TYPES should be extended rather than continuing to hand-verify it run over run.
